3.0.0.en: At the end of the first chapter (ch. 1:17) we learned that Ahaziah son of Ahab had no son, so the kingdom passed after his death to his brother Jehoram son of Ahab. The beginning of his reign over Israel was in the capital Samaria, in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and his rule lasted twelve years. At the time when Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel, it was the second year of Jehoram's sharing the kingdom of Judah with Jehoshaphat his father. Jehoram son of Ahab removed the image of Baal but did not kill the prophets of Baal (v. 13), so the inclination to worship idols remained in Samaria. On the other hand, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah married Athaliah daughter of Ahab, and by this the worship of idols entered the kingdom of Judah. This shows how widespread the worship of idols was in the two Jewish kingdoms, the northern and the southern, in the days of Elisha the prophet, which made his mission difficult in proclaiming the truth and bringing people back to the worship of God.

3.1.0.en: Jehoram was less than his father Ahab and his mother (Jezebel) in irreligion, for he removed the image of Baal that his father had made; yet he did not destroy the prophets of Baal, as is clear from Elisha's reply to him, saying: "Get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother" (v. 13). He gave up outwardly the material appearances of pagan worship, but its spirit remained dominant, and Jehoram did not abandon the national religion founded by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who set up idols in his kingdom at Bethel and Dan (1 Kgs 12:29).

3.1.1.en: Jehoram removed the image of Baal but did not kill his prophets, nor remove the images of the calves at Bethel and Dan. So do not abandon one sin and keep the rest of the sins, for they will drag you into every evil. Offer complete repentance, confident of the power of God, which will support your weakness and free you from the dominion of the sins that rule over you. However often you fall, rise again, insisting on the new life, and God will value your labor and will give you a place in His Kingdom.

3.2.0.en: Mesha king of Moab used to pay tribute to Ahab from his great wealth in livestock, rendering him every year a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams with their wool. This payment of tribute began in the days of Omri king of Israel, but when Ahab died Moab rebelled and no longer paid the tribute.

3.3.0.en: Jehoram was troubled, when he became king after Ahaziah, by the rebellion of Moab and their not paying the tribute to his brother Ahaziah. So he decided to subdue them to himself so that they would pay the tribute, and began to prepare for war. He ordered the numbering of his soldiers to know the fighting strength he possessed, and found it too small for fighting Moab; therefore he thought of allying with other kings to help him in this war.

3.4.0.en: Jehoram king of Israel sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah asking him to ally with him to fight the king of Moab, especially as there was kinship between them, since Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat had married Athaliah the sister of Jehoram king of Israel. Jehoshaphat at once declared his agreement and readiness to fight side by side with the armies of Israel and to share the same dangers for soldiers and horses. Although Jehoshaphat was a good king, he erred in marrying his son to the daughter of Ahab the wicked king of Israel, and then in agreeing to fight with Jehoram king of Israel, because of his attachment to the worship of idols. He had agreed before to fight with Ahab, his father, at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kgs 22:4).

3.5.0.en: Jehoram king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, who had agreed to ally with him to fight the king of Moab, and said to him, Which way shall we go up? There were two roads. The easy road was to go east to the Jordan River and cross it, then descend south and find Moab; or they could go south and pass through Edom and go around from west to east south of the Dead Sea, to fight Moab from the south. This was the hard road, and Jehoshaphat preferred that they take the hard road for the following reasons:

3.5.1.en: 1- Because Moab would not expect them to come by this road, so their attack on Moab would be a surprise, and they would overcome it.

3.5.2.en: 2- Because on the way they would pass through Edom, which was subject to the king of Judah, and would join it with its armies to them, so the alliance would become threefold and stronger.

3.6.0.en: The king of Israel went there in company with his two allies, the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they wandered through the wide desert for seven days without finding a source of water, and the army ran out of water, so that none was left for the soldiers or for the beasts that accompanied the army.

3.6.1.en: It is noted that the kings erred in not praying before going out to war, and consequently did not receive God's help and guidance. They forgot to carry with them plenty of water sufficient for their long journey, or did not calculate carefully their need for water.

3.6.2.en: Do not be so occupied with the problem that faces you and with your plans to solve it that you forget to pray, for God's guidance and help are the foundation of success, and He keeps you from many dangers you do not expect. He loves you, so why do you neglect Him? He will give to you and will take nothing from you, so let Him into your life and into all your needs.

3.7.0.en: Because Jehoram king of Israel had turned away from God and was attached to the worship of idols, when he and the allied armies were exposed to thirst and death he feared God greatly, and because he felt the multitude of his sins he expected this death by thirst to be by God's arrangement, so that the armies of the allies would fall before Moab, for the soldiers would faint from thirst and fall in the war. The man far from God despairs quickly, but the one who believes in God takes refuge in Him and asks His help.

3.8.0.en: If the king of Israel fell into despair and complaint, Jehoshaphat king of Judah, who knows God, noticed that this problem had happened because they had not sought God before going out to war. So he asked those around him, Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may inquire of the Lord by him? One of the servants of Joram king of Israel came forward and said that Elisha the prophet, who had been a disciple and servant of Elijah, was in a nearby place. It is strange that Elisha should be in this place, because they were in the wilderness south of the Dead Sea, far from the northern kingdom of Israel and also south of the southern kingdom, the kingdom of Judah. Most likely the Spirit of God moved Elisha to accompany these soldiers, and he was near their place in the wilderness when they suffered thirst, so that when Jehoshaphat asked for him he would find him.

3.8.1.en: Of course the pagan king of Edom did not care about asking a prophet of God, while Joram king of Israel did not like to see Elisha, because his master Elijah was the one who prophesied about the death of his brother Ahaziah the king before him, and of his father and mother, Ahab and Jezebel; in addition he was occupied with the worship of idols and did not care to hear the voice of God from the tongue of His prophets.

3.9.0.en: Jehoshaphat rejoiced at the news of Elisha's presence and said at once, The word of the Lord is with him, that is, he had found the means by which to hear the voice of God. This shows his godliness and his love for God. He arose to go to him with humility, because he was the one in need of God and of His prophet, and the other two kings, Jehoram king of Israel and the king of Edom, went down with him.

3.10.0.en: Elisha spoke with courage, because the Spirit of God was in him, who had been in Elijah, with a doubled power. He rebuked Jehoram king of Israel, declaring his refusal to cooperate with him because he relied on the prophets of Baal, whom his parents Ahab and Jezebel had cared for and looked after. Although Joram was a Jew, he was attached to the worship of idols; and although he had removed the image of Baal, he still kept the prophets of Baal as his counselors. Even if he was doubtful about the worship of Baal, he was still insistent on that worship. Elisha's words show that God rejects the one who mixes His worship with the worship of idols. It is possible that he had brought with his army some of the prophets of Baal and their images, and asked them to rescue him from death by thirst and they did not rescue him; therefore he refused to consult them again when Elisha told him to go back to them.

3.10.1.en: It is noted that Elisha did not speak to the king of Edom, because he was a pagan and consequently rejects the worship of God. Why then did he come with the two to seek God's counsel? Of course he did not believe in God nor in hearing His voice. But Joram king of Israel answered Elisha that he would not go to the prophets of Baal, and that he felt despair, because he and all his soldiers were suffering thirst and were exposed to destruction at the hand of the king of Moab. This answer shows Jehoram's lack of trust in the idols he worshipped, otherwise he would have resorted to them; and at the same time he felt that by worshipping idols he angered God, so despair overcame him.

3.10.2.en: Rely on God alone and do not be troubled by whatever problems face you. If you use any means to solve the problem, that is only your duty, which you ought to perform; but be confident that the solution will come from God. Any means is worthless as long as you do not trust the power of God that is with you.

3.11.0.en: Elisha swore by God, declaring by this that He is the only God and that the pagan gods are not gods. In the oath Elisha shows that he feels the presence of God and consequently the fear of Him, so he does not fear people, even if they are kings, because God is the Lord of hosts, that is, in Him is the fullness of power, and whoever stands before God has no fear of human power. This oath is the one his master Elijah the prophet always used, for he had been a good disciple at his hands. Elisha declared that for the sake of honoring Jehoshaphat he would convey the voice of God to the kings, so that because of the presence of righteous Jehoshaphat, Joram and the king of Edom would receive a blessing. On the other hand, despite Jehoshaphat's godliness, his carelessness in associating with the kings of Israel, whether Joram or his father Ahab, brought troubles upon him, for which God reproached him.

3.11.1.en: Look for your friends and choose them carefully, so that they may lift you up and support you on the way to the Kingdom, and beware of evil company, for it will certainly influence you, even if partially. If you are bound to them by work or neighborhood, let it be within the narrowest limits, and do not open your heart to them, lest their evil thoughts defile it.

3.12.0.en: Elisha asked for a man to play music on the harp, so that it might accompany his praises raised before God, and after these prayers and praises the Spirit of God came upon him and guided him with the word of God. Prayers and praises are what prepare the heart to hear the voice of God. Indeed, prayer is a dialogue between man and God, in which man lifts up his heart and glorifies God, and God guides him to the truth and good conduct.

3.12.1.en: These praises, on the other hand, drive away demons. If there are those who worship idols, like the king of Edom and the king of Israel and the prophets of Baal who follow them, their power is nullified and their demons flee, so the atmosphere is cleansed and the word of God appears. This was repeated when David the prophet played on the harp and the demons that were in Saul the king fled (1 Sam 16:23). The prophets in the school of the prophets had been accustomed since the days of Samuel to use musical instruments, such as the harp, when praising God (1 Sam 10:5); therefore Elisha asked for a harpist to lift up his praises to God.

3.13.0.en: Ditches: plural of a ditch, which is a well or a pit for keeping water.

3.13.1.en: God's command by the mouth of Elisha the prophet to the kings and those with them was to make in the valley where they stood many deep ditches to receive water. This was a strange command, which human reason does not accept, since there was no source of water and no expectation of rain falling. But this is a proof of faith and submission to God, and God requires this submission in order to work His miracles and pour out His goodness on man. Human striving is a necessary condition for receiving the grace of God, just as Christ asked them to take away the stone from the door of the tomb, and then He worked the miracle and raised Lazarus.

3.14.0.en: God confirms the importance of the faith He asks of His children. He promises them much water that will fill the valley, though they will not see any natural source of water, for the expected source would be rain from heaven and what accompanies the falling of rain, namely wind. What was required of them was faith and carrying out God's command by digging the ditches; then they would enjoy watering and be satisfied with water, they and their beasts.

3.15.0.en: God declared to them that if they believed they would see the valley filled with water and would drink. When they see this miracle they will be sure that it is very easy for God to give them victory over Moab, for their faith will grow and they will not fear the enemies.

3.15.1.en: I wish you would understand God's works and the goodness He gives you, and contemplate His care and thank Him always, so that your faith may be firm and not shaken before any trials or problems that may come upon you.

3.16.0.en: Stop up: to fill in, that is, to fill them with earth and stones.

3.16.1.en: As a result of the multitude of the evils of the Moabites and their immersion in the worship of the pagan god Chemosh, God decided to destroy them severely, that perhaps they would believe in His power and leave the worship of idols. So He asked the three kings, by the mouth of Elisha, to destroy all the fenced and chief cities of the Moabites and to fell every good tree. They were also to stop all the wells of water and to mar the fertility of the land of the fields by casting stones on it.

3.17.0.en: In the morning, at the holy time when the burnt offering is offered on God's altar in Jerusalem, which is a type of Christ the crucified Redeemer, by whose redemption all good things overflow upon humanity, at this time the kings and those with them saw abundant waters coming from the direction of the mountains of Edom, where the rains had fallen, which the kings had not seen, but it was abundant and reached them in the morning and filled the ditches that they had dug in the valley. Then they all drank and rejoiced and thanked God, for they believed, because of this miracle, that God alone is the true God who works miracles, and the pagan gods became small in their eyes. It is understood, of course, that the kings did not offer a sacrifice, but at the time of the offering of the sacrifice in Jerusalem the flowing of water toward the valley took place, for God wants to bind them to Jerusalem and His holy temple, which is the source of all blessings.

3.18.1.en: When the Moabites sensed the movements of the armies of the three kings advancing toward them, they prepared to meet them, gathering on the border everyone able to put on armor, both the conscripts and those older than they who were able to bear arms, that is, they gathered the greatest number of their men because they felt the danger of the armies coming against them.

3.19.0.en: At the time when the waters came from Edom and filled the valley, the Moabites saw the waters red as blood, because the sands of Edom are red, and the water coming from there carries these sands, so its color appears red, in addition to the reflection of the rays of the sun on these waters, so the water appeared like blood.

3.19.1.en: The Moabites were hoping for victory over the alliance of the armies coming against them, so in their pride they imagined that the kings had been divided against one another and had fought, and the blood of their soldiers had flowed and filled the valley. The proud man falls easily into what he imagines, however far from reality. Therefore when the Moabites saw the sight of the blood they had imagined, they rushed in pride to seize the spoil of the allied armies, which they thought had fled after dividing and killing one another.

3.19.2.en: Thus we see God's wonderful arrangement, which led the armies to this valley (v. 16) in Edom so that it would be easy to dig the ditches in it and the rain waters would flow toward it coming from the mountains of Edom, so that the army and its livestock could drink; and at the same time God tests the army's faith in digging the ditches before the waters came, then turns the sight of the waters before the eyes of the enemies into blood, so that they imagine the kings have fought one another and rush in to take their spoil. God mocks the enemies who come against His children and makes them fall in their own evils.

3.19.3.en: The valley signifies humility, and the digging of the ditches to keep the water signifies caring for God's gifts and keeping them, as the disciples gathered the fragments when the multitudes were fed (Mt 14:20). The coming of the waters in abundance signifies God's generosity in His gifts to His children, so that they suffice them and overflow.

3.20.0.en: The Moabites indeed set out to the camp of Israel, to plunder and not to fight, and were surprised by the attack of the allied armies upon them. Before this unexpected attack the Moabites could not hold together, so they fled in fear and panic to their land, and the Israelites pursued them, killing everyone who fell into their hands.

3.21.0.en: Slingers: plural of sling, which is an instrument for throwing stones.

3.21.1.en: Kir-haraseth: the old capital of Moab. Its place today is the city of "Karak" in Jordan, about eighteen kilometers east of the southern part of the Dead Sea.

3.21.2.en: The army of the kings in its advance was destroying the cities, and every soldier cast stones on the arable lands and fruitful fields until they were spoiled. They also stopped all the wells of water and felled every good tree, and nothing remained but the capital of the Moabites, called Kir-haraseth. This was a fortified city with walls built of stones, so it was not easy to demolish them, but the soldiers who use slings advanced and cast many stones upon it to ruin it.

3.22.0.en: Drew swords: trained in the use of swords.

3.22.1.en: When Moab found the allied armies victorious over him, he tried to save the situation by allying with the king of Edom, with whom he had had relations before (2 Chr 20:22, 23). So the king of Moab took seven hundred fighting men of his trained soldiers and tried to break a way for himself through the allied armies, especially the armies of Judah and Israel, so as to reach the king of Edom and ally with him, and by this alliance be able to stand against Judah and Israel allied together; but he failed to break through the ranks of his enemies.

3.22.2.en: God was with the allied armies, so the enemies' attempts failed. Be confident that as long as God is with you, the threats or wrongs of others will not affect you.

3.23.0.en: Then the king of Moab took his eldest son and offered him for a burnt offering upon the wall of the city to the idol Chemosh, the god of the Moabites. The people of the children of Israel shuddered at this dreadful sight and raised the siege and withdrew, returning to their homes without any celebration of victory. Perhaps the king of Moab thought that the withdrawal of the kings meant victory for him, and that it was because of the human sacrifice he had offered to his gods; but in reality he remained defeated amid the ruin and destruction that had come upon his cities.

3.23.1.en: Perhaps the allied armies felt that this victory was enough for them, that is, the offering as a sacrifice of the enemy's crown prince, who was reigning with his father and in his place, so they departed.

3.23.2.en: "There was great indignation against Israel" happened, that is, Edom and Judah were indignant at Israel, who caused the crown prince to be offered as a sacrifice, and this displeasure made them depart from the king of Israel who had drawn them into this war. In general the war ended, but Moab had been laid waste, as divine discipline, and at the same time the power of God appeared, which supported the allied armies because of the presence of believing Jehoshaphat with them.

3.23.3.en: The departure of Edom and Judah from Israel signifies that the outward worship that Israel offers, while it mixes its worship of God with idols, makes the pagans in the end turn away from it, and those who worship God turn away from it also.

3.23.4.en: Do not try to mix your way as a child of God with the evil ways of the world, for the world will not be pleased with you and God will of course be angry with you. Do not be lukewarm but hot, so that you may receive God's power and blessing and find your salvation.
